source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Description , Turn on the system and enter Setup. Enter the "Integrated Devices" menu in Setup.
Input Data
The menu should include a field named "OS Watchdog Timer".

2
Description
Select the OS Watchdog Timer field and press F1.
Input Data
The help text for the Watchdog Timer field should read:
"If your system stops responding, this watchdog timer aids in the recovery of your operating system. When this field is set to Enabled, the operating system is allowed to initialize the timer. When it is set to Disabled (the default), the timer will have no effect on the system."

3 Description
Press Esc to exit the help text. Press the arrow keys to scroll through all the selections for the field.
Input Data
The selections for the field should be "Enabled" and "Disabled".

4 Description
Set the field to "Enabled", then press Alt-F.
Input Data
The field should switch to "Disabled" since this is the default setting.

5 Description
Set the OS Watchdog Timer field to "Enabled". Save the change and reboot. Using an ICE, stop the system just before it is about to execute int 19h to boot.
Using the ICE, view the Watchdog Resource Table (WDAT) in the F000h block (the address of this table can be found in the BIOS.MAP file at the "WDAT" label).
Input Data
Offset 03Ch, bit 0 in the WDAT should be 1 since the Watchdog Timer is enabled in Setup.

6 Description
Reboot the system, enter Setup, and set the OS Watchdog Timer field to "Disabled". Save the change and reboot. Using an ICE, stop the system just before it is about to execute int 19h to boot.
Again, view memory at the address of the Watchdog Resource Table (WDAT) in the F000h block.
Input Data
This time, the table "WDAT" should not exist since the Watchdog Timer is "Disabled" in Setup.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: operator to cut AC + BMC creds
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- AC drop 3 times: perform 3 AC drops (operator cuts AC then drops it back) and confirm the host/BMC recover. Agent logs host boot + BMC SEL after each drop; the physical AC action is operator-only.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return post-drop host boot marker + ipmitool -I lanplus -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" sel elist 2>&1 | tail -30 so the user confirms clean recovery after each AC drop (3x); physical action is operator-performed.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: AC drop is physical + can lose unsaved state; operator performs the AC cut on a dedicated SUT.
deepseek_columns.remark: same code in 2 workbook rows (multi-row code)

original_test_intent: Manually verify the BIOS OS Watchdog control, help/options/default, and state-dependent WDAT firmware representation using an approved ICE/debug setup.
original_method: A trained engineer navigates BIOS, toggles the setting, reboots and halts pre-boot execution with ICE to inspect firmware memory/table state.
manual_activity: BIOS navigation, ICE halt/memory inspection and interpretation are the core acceptance and must be performed by a qualified engineer; the agent can organize exported evidence only.
required_inputs: WDAT address/offset/bit semantics for both states
Stable power, console recovery and restore state
safety_requirements: Use ICE read-only and never write firmware memory.
Reject physical AC drops as a substitute.
Maintain console/recovery and stable power for debug halts.
No automatic retry; restore approved watchdog setting.
agent_execution_scope: Prepare evidence checklist and compare exported screenshots/dumps with the owner baseline.
Do not operate BIOS/ICE, claim observation or issue verdict.
engineer_actions: Perform BIOS and ICE steps, verify memory/table evidence and restore setting.

command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain the approved manual BIOS/ICE method; use offline parsing only for exported dumps.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All six BIOS/ICE steps, offset 03Ch bit 0 and 10/10 minutes remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Record BIOS UI states, use a validated read-only ICE to capture WDAT in both states, correlate BIOS.MAP and restore the approved default.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact BIOS build and debug hardware.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BIOS, ACPI/WDAT revision, ICE firmware/tool version.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform BIOS watchdog and debug documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Only adds provenance and restoration evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No replacement of the firmware-memory inspection.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Platform WDAT contract and ICE package.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A debug halt can interrupt boot or destabilize a service system.

project_override_considerations: A documented firmware-table dump may be accepted by a project only if it proves the same pre-boot state and coverage; record the override.
expected_evidence: Enabled-state WDAT dump and bit decoding

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The code is reused at row 1526 for unrelated AC drop 3 times, and same-row DeepSeek imports that method; the XLSX BIOS/ICE scope is authoritative.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The source procedure and criteria align. Required platform/debug inputs affect readiness, while the core remains MANUAL ONLY.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Explicitly separates manual observation from offline agent assistance.

review_improvement: Preserves state-dependent WDAT evidence and blocks both firmware writes and unrelated power cycling.
independent_technical_reasoning: The acceptance depends on interactive BIOS UI and pre-boot ICE memory inspection; these are engineer-operated observations, not an automatable runtime software test.
